questions.q: In an Order-to-Cash scenario, where does the data on the Receivables invoice primarily come from?
options: A billing clerk typing each line by hand from scratch
The customer's own accounting system
The order and the confirmed shipment, carried forward automatically
A random default template
questions.explain: The invoice is generated from data that already originated in Order Management and Shipping, not re-typed by a clerk.

questions.q: What determines the unit price that appears on SO-48217's invoice?
options: The order line's negotiated price, including the 5% discount already applied
A brand-new price entered during invoicing
The customer's credit limit
The General Ledger period
questions.explain: The invoice carries forward the order line's already-discounted negotiated price.

questions.q: What is the difference between an invoice's transaction date and its GL date?
options: There is no difference, they are always identical
Transaction date is set by the customer
GL date is only used for purchase orders
Transaction date reflects when invoicing happened; GL date determines which accounting period the journal entry posts to
questions.explain: Transaction date reflects the invoicing event; GL date controls which period the resulting accounting lands in, and they can diverge.

questions.q: What determines the quantity that appears on the invoice?
options: The quantity originally requested, regardless of what shipped
The confirmed shipped quantity
A random sample of the order
The customer's payment history
questions.explain: Quantity invoiced comes from the confirmed shipped quantity, which can differ from the originally requested quantity.

questions.q: What does this lesson assume you already know from the Accounts Receivable course?
options: Nothing about Receivables at all
How to configure a chart of accounts
The basic structure of a Receivables transaction/invoice: type, bill-to, lines, terms, due date
How Oracle Fusion handles fixed assets
questions.explain: This lesson builds on the already-covered Receivables transaction structure rather than re-teaching it from scratch.
